rationale: Both responses give a credible end-to-end design: multi-task urgency plus finding heads, calibration, patient-level validation, a DICOM gateway such as Orthanc, Triton or FastAPI serving, DICOM SR write-back, HL7 or FHIR to the RIS, and FDA Class II framing. A's PACS section, which the prompt specifically asks about, contains several fabricated or wrong specifics an engineer could act on: nonexistent HL7 message types ('ORU^OBS', 'ORU^RSL', where results are ORU^R01 and orders ORM/OMI), a made-up vendor ('VitalPics'), the idea of 'registering' a LOINC code, and a 'no HTTP' claim that conflicts with its own DICOMweb use. B uses correct DICOMweb verbs (QIDO, WADO, STOW) and ORU^R01, and discusses push versus polling triggers, large-study retrieval, cloud versus hybrid PACS, and de-identification at the gateway. It also frames the recall-versus-false-positive asymmetry well, adds 2D-versus-3D and specialist-ensemble choices, external validation with expected degradation, and a phased build plan. B has its own errors: it cites the wrong DICOM part for de-identification, and its suggestion that hospitals can deploy as unregulated CDS is questionable. Overall it is more accurate and more complete.
